title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in: Silvercrest Capital
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in: Silvercrest is evaluating a dedicated capacity upgrade and adding eu-west region for data residency. Security team validated SOC 2 posture but requested KMS/HSM integration details and audit log retention info. AE to send updated SOW and tiered pricing for 6/12 month commits; SE to run targeted throughput benchmarks with their 8k token seqs and share results next week.
next_steps: Dana to share updated SOW + tiered pricing by 2026-05-11
Liam to run benchmark (8k seqs, 50 concurrent) on Dedicated and share results by 2026-05-15
Aisha to provide compliance checklist and target audit retention requirements by 2026-05-12
Schedule technical deep-dive for KMS/HSM integration with infra team week of 2026-05-18

Liam Chen - Run throughput & latency benchmarks (8k token, 50 concurrent) and upload results - due: 2026-05-15

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Dana Ortiz, Liam Chen (Redwood); Maya Patel, Carlos Romero, Aisha Khan (Silvercrest)

[00:00] Dana Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:05] Maya Patel: Yeah all good. Thanks Dana. We pulled you on because renewal window coming up and we also want to scope the capacity bump and the EU region.
[00:12] Dana Ortiz: Perfect. Quick agenda: renewal timing, dedicated capacity options (we heard H100 pool), regional expansion to eu-west-1, and any compliance open items. Liam will jump in for technical detail.
[00:22] Carlos Romero: Sounds good. Our timeline is roughly end of May for a signed extension if possible, but we can be flexible depending on pricing. We want to add an additional 8 GPUs equivalent - basically move from our current 4x A100 reserved to an 8x H100 pool.
[00:35] Liam Chen: Right, an 8x H100 dedicated pool will give you a big jump in throughput but we should validate with your 8k token sequences; latency will depends on batching and KV cache hits.
[00:45] Maya Patel: Yeah our main workload has long context transcripts and a lot of prefix reuse so cache hit rate is pretty high. The big ask is predicting cost per 1M tokens and the SLO for p95 latency.
[00:55] Liam Chen: For that workload we generally see 30-40% token cost reduction moving to H100 with the optimized kernels, plus our continuous batching helps. For p95 latency, with an 8x pool and your traffic shape I expect mid-200ms to sub-400ms for 2k-3k generation slices; the 8k sequences will be higher - we'll run bench.
[01:12] Aisha Khan: From security perspective, SOC 2 is fine, but we need details on KMS integration and HSM key control. We can't have keys stored in Redwood-managed KMS for EU data.
[01:22] Dana Ortiz: Understood. We support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations in Private deployments and with Dedicated we have options: you can bring your key via our KMS proxy or opt for on-prem key-stores. We'll provide the architecture doc.
[01:32] Aisha Khan: Also audit log retention - we need 7 years for some of our workflows. Is that in scope?
[01:37] Dana Ortiz: Audit logs can be exported to your S3 and we can set retention. For Hosted API we have 90 day default, but for Dedicated/Private we can configure long-term retention. We'll note that.
[01:45] Carlos Romero: Great. On the EU region: we must keep eu customer data in eu-west-1. Can Redwood spin up dedicated region there? What's the lead time?
[01:53] Liam Chen: We have an eu-west-1 region available for Dedicated customers. Provisioning a new dedicated pool in eu-west typically takes 2-3 weeks depending on capacity, network peering, and infra approvals. If you're adding GPUs and want an on-prem style VPC peering, plan for three weeks.
[02:06] Maya Patel: Ok, so if we sign end of May, feasibility wise we could have it by mid-June?
[02:10] Liam Chen: That's plausible, assuming the contract and network details are cleared quickly. We'll also need to run a baseline benchmark in eu-west because hardware variants and kernel choices can change perf numbers slightly.
[02:20] Dana Ortiz: Quick callout on pricing: we can offer tiered reserved pricing for 6 vs 12 month commits. 12-month gives the best unit price and priority capacity allocation for region provisioning. I'll send a draft SOW with the tiers after this call.
[02:33] Carlos Romero: We might prefer a 6-month initial commit with an option to extend to 12. Need to show finance the delta.
[02:39] Dana Ortiz: Totally. We'll include an option line item for extend-to-12 with pro-rated credit mechanics.
[02:45] Maya Patel: For the pilot benchmarking, Liam, can you run our 8k seqs at 50 concurrency? That's what we see in peak batch windows.
[02:53] Liam Chen: Yep, we can replicate that. A couple notes: we'll need a sample prompt set and example payloads (especially to approximate CPU pre/post processing). If you can drop a sanitized sample to the shared folder we'll use it. Also, are you using long LLMs or mostly 2-turn chat comps?
[03:10] Maya Patel: Mostly long single-shot generations, with some system-level priming reused across requests. So KV cache will be effective.
[03:18] Aisha Khan: On the KMS note, we need to see the detailed flow: key import/export prevention, attestation, and whether Redwood has access to plaintext. We can't allow any plaintext keys outside our control.
[03:28] Liam Chen: Under Dedicated we never have access to your plaintext keys if you use the bring-your-own approach - the KMS proxy routes requests and Redwood only sees encrypted artifacts. We'll put together a diagram and reference our compliance docs.
[03:38] Dana Ortiz: I'll attach the KMS/HSM integration diagram and the SOC 2 section in a follow-up email.
[03:44] Carlos Romero: Another item: network egress costs. We host some of our clients in EU; if we process in eu-west that reduces egress but we've had surprises historically. How are egress billing and peering set?
[03:53] Dana Ortiz: Egress billing depends on how traffic flows. With direct VPC peering you avoid public egress and incur internal transfer only. We'll include network topologies and estimated egress for the eu deployment in the SOW.
[04:04] Maya Patel: Awesome. A practical question: can we burst to extra capacity for heavy days? We occasionally have big spike windows.
[04:12] Liam Chen: Yes, we offer burst policies and autoscaling for Dedicated: you can reserve baseline capacity and allow bursts to a higher tier, subject to available global spare capacity. That can be set up in the policy and tied to cost controls.
[04:23] Maya Patel: Good. For our compliance sign-off we also need IP protection and code-of-conduct for the models - basically we need to know where models are stored, any third-party transfer, and model weights custody.
[04:33] Dana Ortiz: We can provide a model custody doc. For curated open models we list the upstream provenance; weights remain in the customer's dedicated pool and are not exported. If you use hosted shared models, those are in Redwood-managed catalog. We'll flag that in the doc.
[04:45] Carlos Romero: One minor thing: last quarter we saw a regression in quality after a quantization change in a test branch. How do rollbacks and canary are handled during model variant changes?
[04:56] Liam Chen: We have rollback and canary rollouts in the console - you can do percentage-based traffic splits, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. For quantization-based variants we run offline evals and also tie regressions to prompt sets. We'll show you the rollout UI in the next demo.
[05:09] Maya Patel: That would help. Also, we've got a small legal ask: can you include an SLA clause for latency p95 for our tier?
[05:16] Dana Ortiz: For Dedicated we can commit to latency targets in the SLA with penalties for missed SLOs. We'll draft language aligned with the pool size and traffic profile.
[05:24] Aisha Khan: For audit purposes, can you provide example logs that show token-level latencies and which model variant served the request? We need that for forensic tracing.
[05:33] Liam Chen: Yes, we emit per-request metadata including model id, variant, token tally, and latency buckets to the audit stream. We'll include sample logs (sanitized).
[05:42] Dana Ortiz: Quick check - anything else on compliance or procurement?
[05:45] Aisha Khan: Procurement wants a standard MSA and data processing addendum. We prefer Reed & Gray MSA template but we can accept Redwood's with a few edits.
[05:54] Dana Ortiz: We'll include our standard MSA + DPA and mark the editable areas. If you pass over the Reed & Gray redline we'll align on the changes.
[06:02] Carlos Romero: Ok good. On pricing again, will we get a discount for committing to both region expansion and capacity?
[06:08] Dana Ortiz: Yes, multi-region + capacity commits can be bundled for an additional discount. We'll surface bundle options in the SOW and show prorated extension logic.
[06:16] Maya Patel: Liam - for the benchmark, what metrics will you report? We want median/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), cost per 1M tokens estimate, and GPU utilization.
[06:25] Liam Chen: We'll provide median/p95 latency, tokens/sec for generation and end-to-end (including pre/post processing), GPU power and memory utilization, and the cost per 1M tokens under the proposed reserved pricing.
[06:36] Maya Patel: Great. We'll put together a sanitized sample payloads link after this.
[06:40] Carlos Romero: Also schedule-wise, if we sign at the end of May can you start billing from June 1 for committed capacity? We prefer start-of-month billing.
[06:48] Dana Ortiz: Yes we can align billing to start of month for committed capacity if contract executed before month end. We'll include that option.
[06:55] Aisha Khan: One more security question: are keys ever backed up to US regions if we use eu region? We need assurance of strict region residency for key backups.
[07:03] Liam Chen: If you opt for customer-managed KMS in eu-west we can keep backups in eu-west only; we won't replicate keys to US unless you request cross-region backup. We'll document backup policies.
[07:14] Maya Patel: Fantastic. Any risks you foresee in the rollout?
[07:18] Liam Chen: Main risks: network peering delays, capacity availability in the exact sku of H100 in eu-west, and any unexpected throughput differences with 8k sequences - all manageable with early coordination.
[07:29] Dana Ortiz: Ok wrapping up, recap: Dana sends SOW + tiered pricing and network topologies; Liam runs benchmarks and shares results; Silvercrest provides sample payloads and compliance checklist.
[07:39] Carlos Romero: Yep that's the plan. We'll try to get the Reed & Gray redline to you by next week.
[07:44] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone.
[07:46] Dana Ortiz: Thanks all, I'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep-dive for KMS with Liam.
[07:52] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (e.g., A100 vs H100, KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash"). References: SOW draft link (internal): https://redwood.example.com/sow/silvercrest-draft (placeholder), security deck: https://redwood.example.com/security/silvercrest (placeholder).
